ask_parts_not_covered.why: no check exists for a human approving an action; AGENT-020 only checks that a named approval function is called, not that it runs before the email or that a person approved

ask_parts_not_covered.part: AI tools cannot call tools the owner has not given

ask_parts_not_covered.part: AI tools cannot delete anything (only the delete statements listed)
ask_parts_not_covered.why: partly covered: the check lists delete, truncate and raw SQL names; a delete via a named statement outside this list would pass

assumptions: AI tools that email customers are tagged sends-email (tag does not exist yet)
approval function is named request_human_approval (does not exist yet)
the owner's delete statements are db.del, db.bulk.delete, db.truncate, db.direct_query (names confirmed from catalogue text, not from a workspace)
no email statement name is needed because outbound.vendor_allowlist was not used
confusions: No check or template for human-in-the-loop approval, so the approval rule is a proxy that cannot prove approval happened.
stack.statement_order would enforce approval before an email but needs an exact email statement name, which the catalogue does not list (only provider kinds). I did not guess one.
The AI-tool-allowlist half of the ask has no check at all, and the skill does not say to say so before writing rules; I had to infer that from the catalogue's agent and tool object kinds.
Tag-scoped rules are inert until the tag exists; the skill says propose such tags separately, but the reply has to say the rule matches nothing yet.
wished_for: a check or template for human approval before a tool performs an action
a check that compares an agent's enabled tools to an allowlist
the list of email statement names, and a recipe for ordering approval before them
a recipe for a tool-scoped rule that does not need a new tag
parse_errors_seen: AGENT-020.R1: tags sends-email is on no tool on this branch
AGENT-020.R1: Function request_human_approval is not on this branch
why_confidence: The delete half is well covered by a check. The approval half is only a proxy, email ordering is not checked, and the tool allowlist half has no check at all, so the policy does not achieve the goal as asked.
